messages:
mika: Drafting a proposal for header-based routing precedence. Goal: allow gateway-signed headers to route to dedicated pools, fall back to UA inference, and reject customer-controlled routing unless authenticated. PTAL.

Config sketch:
```
match:
  headers:
    - name: X-Cust-Type
      value: premium|enterprise
  user_agent: /RedwoodSDK\/\d+\.\d+/
route: dedicated-pool
fallback:
  headers:
    - name: X-Signed-Route
      verify: true
```

Questions: precedence rules, spoof risk mitigations, telemetry tags, and quota semantics.

devin: I think signed header should have top precedence if signature verifies. Otherwise UA inference wins. We should avoid relying on raw X-Customer-* headers unless the auth token matches.

raj: Agree re: spoofing. Customer headers are untrusted. We should prefer claims in the bearer token (customer_id, tier) or a gateway-stamped header. If accepting X-Signed-Route, require HMAC signed by gateway key and short TTL.

sasha: How do we surface this in dashboards? If routing decisions flip based on UA vs signed header, we need a tag for route_source so billing/latency dashboards can group correctly. Also what happens to quotas—per-customer vs per-route?

mika: Proposed practical rules:
1) If X-Signed-Route present and signature valid -> route per signed value. Stamp x-route-source=gateway-signed.
2) Else if auth token includes customer_id and tier -> route by token claim. Stamp x-route-source=auth-claim.
3) Else if UA matches RedwoodSDK and includes sdk-tier -> soft-route via UA inference (best-effort). Stamp x-route-source=ua-infer.
4) Else default to shared-pool.

For signature: header format `X-Signed-Route: sig=<b64>,ts=<unix>` and verification at edge: `verify_hmac(key, route||ts)`. Reject if ts skew > 60s.

devin: Also recommend a numeric x-customer-priority header that only gateway may set for admission control (soft routing), and never accept it from raw client. Use it to bias batch allocation, not to bypass quotas.

raj: Gateway should also stamp `x-auth-ctx` with a compact base64(json) including minimal claims {cid, tier, exp} so downstream services can make auth-aware decisions without re-parsing tokens. Only gateway and internal clients can set this. Reject any incoming x-auth-ctx unless gateway-signed.

cicd-bot: deploy scheduled: header-routing-gatekeepers -> staging @ 03:00 UTC (canary 5%). :rocket:

gateway-oncall: Heads-up: we had an incident last quarter where UA sniffing caused mis-routing when a third-party crawler set a mobile UA that matched our regex. Add sampling logs for decisions and an allowlist for known SDK client strings. Also add metric `routing.decision_override` for alerting.

sasha: Sounds good. For telemetry: add tags `route_source`, `route_decision`, `route_signature_ok` to tracing spans and metrics. Quota semantics: default to token-claim customer quotas; when UA-infer used, attribute to 'inferred' bucket and apply conservative shared limits.

mika: Next steps: write RFC with examples, define header formats (X-Signed-Route, X-Route-Stamp, X-Auth-Ctx), add gateway stamp + verifier, implement canary in staging with 5% traffic, wire up tracing tags and dashboards, and create alerts for routing override rates.

Please ack with :+1: or comment if you want different ordering. I'll open RFC today.
